newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen resist JGB surge but hold firm.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen resist JGB surge but hold firm.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were firmer in late Tuesday trade but resisted the euphoric momentum of Japanese government bond (JGB) futures which shot to new contract highs after a long weekend.
December JGBs settled at 126.37 against their opening 125.34 after hitting a high of 126.41.
Dealers said talk of public fund buying of cash bonds in the face of continued weakness in the Nikkei underpinned the market.
Rumours of financial difficulties at a small Japanese regional bank and a media report which said the Bank of Japan hoped the JGB market would remain bullish also provided a boost.
"Market participants believe Japanese public funds are buying cash JGBs," said a dealer at a Japanese bank.
"But Euroyen has not moved much because there is no change expected in the BOJ's monetary policy," he said. "The short end of the curve is looking for some news to push it out of its tight range."
The lead June Euroyen contract stood one tick off its intra-day high of 99.39 in late trade against an IMM close at 99.25.
The dealer said expectations of a sell-off in dollar/yen after the U.S. elections would help Euroyen and JGB futures to remain firm.

Dealers said the market was widely expecting President Bill Clinton to be re-elected, but U.S. stock and bond markets could take a beating if the Democrats made a clean sweep in the Congressional race as well.
"The Democrats are not very friendly to business. If they get control of Congress, that would be a problem," said a dealer with a local institution.
